question: How should Agency's MCP server start automatically in any project where Agency is enabled?
context: agency init writes project .mcp.json and .claude/settings.json with absolute paths to this checkout (gitignored, machine-specific). In another app the server fails to start: it needs a Claude Code restart, manual approval, node_modules in the checkout, and a still-valid absolute path.

options.name: Claude Code plugin
options.what_it_is: Package Agency as a Claude Code plugin. Enabling it registers its MCP server, hooks and skill automatically, with no per-project .mcp.json approval.
options.how_it_fits_here: Add .claude-plugin/plugin.json and marketplace.json, a plugin .mcp.json using ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, hooks/hooks.json, and move skills/agency in. Installer shrinks to creating .agency/ only.
pros: Enable means server runs, hooks and skill included
No absolute paths, works on every machine
cons: Claude Code only; Cursor/Codex still need manual MCP config
Dependencies must ship or install on first run
options.reversibility_why: Plugin files are additive; init can stay as fallback.

options.name: Publish to npm, use npx
options.what_it_is: Publish agency as an npm package; init writes .mcp.json with npx so no checkout path is needed.
options.how_it_fits_here: Drop private in package.json, ship prebuilt gui/dist, change src/init.js to emit npx commands for MCP and hooks. Still project-scope .mcp.json needing approval.
cons: Still needs one-time approval and restart
npx cold start slows each session
Must publish and version on npm

recommendation.why: Only option where enabling Agency itself starts the server, hooks and skill, with no approval step or machine-specific paths.
recommendation.would_change_mind_if: Most users run non-Claude clients, then npx wins.
